title: An element cutting the support of a Cohen–Macaulay module by one dimension is a nonzerodivisor on it
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$). For a finite $R$-module $N$ let $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, $N_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\dots\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ ($-\infty$ when $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\emptyset$, i.e. $N=0$; the same definition for any subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in place of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$). Let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $g\in\mathfrak m$ and let $V(g)$ be the set of prime ideals of $R$ containing $g$; suppose that $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)\bigr)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)-1$. Then (a) $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $g$ on $M$ is injective), and (b) $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$.

Rewrite the depth of M using the Cohen–Macaulay equality and the returned depth value, then simplify the natural-number subtraction using 1 ≤ d.
